newsitem.title: USA: Western Pacific to acquire Frontier in stock swap.
newsitem.headline: Western Pacific to acquire Frontier in stock swap.

text.p: Western Pacific Airlines Inc. will acquire Frontier Airlines Inc. in a stock swap valued at about $36.5 million, combining two low-fare Colorado-based carriers, the companies announced Monday.

Western Pacific will exchange three-fourths of a share of its stock for each share of Frontier under the definitive agreement approved by both airlines' boards, the companies said in a joint statement.
The deal will give Frontier stockholders about 31 percent ownership of Colorado Springs, Colo.-based Western Pacific.

"This is an exciting combination that makes great sense for both companies," said Western Pacific Chief Executive Officer Robert Peiser. "In addition to helping us reach a critical mass, combining the carriers will allow us to offer a significant number of flights in each market."

Western Pacific, founded in 1994, has a fleet of 18 Boeing 737-300s and flies to 27 destinations -- including New York, Chicago, Washington, Denver, Dallas, Los Angeles and San Francisco -- in combination with its commuter affiliate, Mountain Air Express. It has 1,326 employees.

Frontier, resurrected in 1993 by several executives from the original Frontier Airlines, has a fleet of seven Boeing 737-200s and four 737-300s. It serves 15 mostly Western and Midwestern destinations, including Denver, Minneapolis, Las Vegas, Chicago and St. Louis. It has 750 employees.
Beginning Aug. 1, the two airlines said they plan to begin an interim arrangement that would offer 76 daily departures from Denver International Airport to 25 destinations.
By year's end the carriers plan to have 86 daily departures serving 26 markets and raise the number of Boeing 737 aircraft they operate to 34 from 30.
Under the deal, three Frontier directors will join Western Pacific's board, which would be expanded to nine members.

Western Pacific stock closed up 12.5 cents at $5.50 Monday on Nasdaq. Frontier fell 12.5 cents to $3.875, also on Nasdaq. With 8.84 million shares of Frontier stock outstanding in June, the deal would be worth about $36.5 million.
The airlines said no decision had been made on what the new company will be called.
